name: dla
description: Detect Leak Anywhere: evidence-gated memory leak diagnosis for JVM, Go, Rust, Node/TS, Python and native code. Diagnosis only; it never edits project source.

redaction.title: Value redaction
redaction.description: How values read from the target are shown to the model: 'shapes' (the default) shows value shapes only, such as length, character pattern and a salted hash. 'raw' takes effect only together with a separate per-run raw-value consent that DLA asks for; without that consent summaries still show shapes.

privilege_ceiling.title: Privilege ceiling
privilege_ceiling.description: Highest privilege tier (1 to 4) that DLA may offer. DLA asks one consent question per run covering tiers 1 to 4, and this ceiling caps which tiers that question can include. Tiers escalate by intrusiveness: 1 builds and runs project code in a scratch copy under the run directory (builds, tests, harness loops, preload agents, in-process probes); 2 observes a running local process DLA did not start (/proc or libproc sampling of a PID, jcmd attach, Node inspector, a Go pprof endpoint); 3 is debugger or kernel level (ptrace attach, eBPF, perf, valgrind, may need root); 4 captures memory contents (heap dumps, heap snapshots, core dumps), whose outputs may contain secrets. The full definitions are in references/safety-and-effects.md. The default is 4.

time_budget.title: Default time budget
time_budget.description: Wall-clock budget for one diagnosis run. The default, auto, starts at 60 minutes and is sized to the project once the sweep has found its candidates (20 minutes plus 15 per runtime and 3 per candidate, between 60 minutes and 3 hours). A fixed value such as 90s, 45m or 2h is also accepted and is never resized.
